status: finite named-candidate font-control review complete; encoding uncertainty explicitly retained, not whole-source installation approval
conclusions: Ordinary হ has a lower tail; this alone never proves hasanta.
Many target glyphs also have a second separate lower stroke. Same-row Bengali হাত versus Chakma/Brokskat হাত, and Santali versus Chakma হাগা, prove a real printed distinction.
Genuine joined হ্ম in ব্রহ্মাণ্ড and হ্য in সহ্য differ from full separate ম/য following disputed target হ.
Clear হুঁ in Bengali হুঁকো has a hooked vowel shape distinct from the extra diagonal; do not retain u merely because OCR guessed it.

The scan and available controls do not securely distinguish every marked-ha encoding from সম্ভাব্য রফলা or author-specific modification. This finite residual uncertainty must be retained, not resolved by phonological inference.
